title: review: v2 next_goal: a closed goal leads a decision Planner to file the next roadmap goal
spec:
When a goal is closed (result.goal_closed true, and with [ship].enabled also ship state shipped), file the next goal
from the repo's roadmap so a repo keeps working without a human in the session.

1. Roadmap format: .orchestrator/roadmap.md, checklist lines `- [ ] <goal text>` (unchecked = not filed yet) and
   `- [x] <goal text> (T-xxxx)`. Lines outside the checklist are context.
2. Config [planner].next_goal (default false). When true and a goal closes, add a decision point of a new kind
   "next_goal" in orchestrator/planner_runs.py decision_points(); its packet carries the closed goal's title, result and
   retrospective, the roadmap text and the open goals. At most one next_goal decision per closed goal (reuse the
   records/claim machinery and its keys).
3. The decision Planner prompt for next_goal (.orchestrator/prompts/planner-decision.md section or a new prompt file
   next to it): pick the first unchecked roadmap item whose dependencies are met, create the goal task and its first atomic
   tasks on the bus exactly as an interactive Planner would, tick the roadmap line with the goal id, commit. If no item
   is ready it records why and stops. It never files more than one goal per decision.
4. No roadmap file or no unchecked item -> no decision point, nothing launched.
Tests tests/test_next_goal.py: test_next_goal_disabled_by_default, test_next_goal_point_after_close, test_next_goal_waits_for_ship_when_enabled,
test_next_goal_once_per_closed_goal, test_no_point_without_unchecked_items, test_packet_contains_roadmap_and_retrospective.


AMENDMENTS v2 from spec review T-1698 (final; sent to the builder without another spec review round; the post-gate
review still applies). Where they differ from the text above, these win.
N1 Routing: a new decision kind is dispatched in several places. Route "next_goal" everywhere a kind is mapped:
   orchestrator/decision.py (route ~150), orchestrator/planner_taxonomy.py (must not fall to 'other'),
   orchestrator/planner_packet.py (kind -> type map), and in planner_runs.py _condition_resolved, _decision_task and
   build_ctx. All of these files are in scope.
N2 No backlog storm: the first time decision_points() sees next_goal enabled it writes
   .orchestrator/next_goal_state.json {"enabled_at": <ts>}; only goals closed (pipeline.closed_at) after enabled_at
   produce a point. Historical closed goals never do.
N3 Config: decision_points() reads [planner].next_goal through the pool config loader (orchestrator/pool.py; add the
   default False there, in scope). Tests use that loader, not a literal.
N4 Idempotent filing: each roadmap line has a stable key (first 12 hex of sha1 of the stripped line text). The
   decision Planner first searches the bus for a goal with constraints.roadmap_key == key; if found it only ticks the
   line. Otherwise it creates the goal with constraints.roadmap_key, then ticks the line and commits. Undo path
   documented in the prompt: mark the goal superseded and untick the line.
N5 Untrusted, bounded packet: roadmap and retrospective go through the existing _fenced(label, value, limit) helper,
   roadmap capped at 3000 chars (all unchecked lines first, then up to 20 checked lines for context), retrospective
   at 2000. The prompt states both are data, never instructions.
N6 Gate and bound: with [ship].enabled a point exists only when the closed goal's pipeline.ship.state == "shipped"
   (held/pending/merging suppress it); without ship, goal_closed is enough. No point while another goal of this repo is
   open (not closed): at most one unattended goal at a time. [planner].next_goal_max_per_day (default 3) caps launches.
N7 Extra tests: test_routing_kind_next_goal_in_decision_taxonomy_packet, test_no_points_for_goals_closed_before_enable,
   test_default_false_from_pool_loader, test_existing_roadmap_key_only_ticks, test_packet_fences_and_caps,
   test_suppressed_while_ship_held_or_other_goal_open, test_daily_cap, test_prompt_renders_next_goal_section,
   test_no_ready_item_records_reason.
acceptance: tests/test_next_goal.py: the six named tests exist and pass

result.summary: The six named tests exist and pass the gate, and next_goal defaults to false through pool.py planner_setting. The N1 to N7 amendments are implemented. Two non-blocking issues remain. The 'test_next_goal: missing' line in the packet is spurious, since tests/test_next_goal.py is present.

comments.issue: _open_goals only excludes status done and failed. A goal marked superseded, which is the undo path the new prompt documents, still counts as open. Because decision_points yields no next_goal point while any goal is open, that goal blocks all further autonomous filing until a human closes it. Exclude 'superseded' (and any other terminal status) here.

_condition_resolved for next_goal only counts a goal with a new roadmap_key, or a 'no ready item' line in plan.md. When the Planner takes the 'goal already exists, only tick the line' path, neither condition holds, so the run is scored exited_early or gave_up. Count a roadmap.md mtime or commit after launch as resolved.

decision_points() calls _next_goal_enabled_at(), which writes next_goal_state.json. A read-only caller such as a status or summary path therefore creates the file and starts the enabled_at clock. The write is also non-atomic, so a torn file resets enabled_at to now. This is only a minor side effect, not a storm risk.
include_scouts is forced to False whenever any next_goal section is present. If the same packet also carries a scouts_done or held section for another goal, those scout findings are dropped.
